operator: hostapd 2.11, dnsmasq 2.92, radvd 2.20, Scapy 2.8.0, OpenSSL 3.5.5, and tcpdump 4.99.6 in an OrbStack Ubuntu 26.04.1 arm64 VM; independent CoreWLAN wildcard scan from macOS 26.3

console.model_source: owner manual confirmation; PTP DeviceInfo reports the generic model 'Nintendo Switch'
console.firmware_observation_note: The console was not involved in Phase 0.
console.modification_source: owner report; this test does not detect modifications

wpa2_ap.hostapd_log_confirms: wpa_version=0x2, PSK derived, group key installed
wpa2_ap.independent_scan_result: seen at -34 dBm on channel 1; a later capture-time scan saw it at -35 dBm

independent_scan.receiver: macOS CoreWLAN wildcard scan with Location Services
independent_scan.bssid_visibility: nil for every network in the returned array; SSID, RSSI, and channel were usable

capture_path.monitor_channel_set_result: EBUSY while the AP held channel 1; the monitor followed the AP channel
capture_path.hostapd_debug_log: recorded probe requests and probe responses, including a probe request at -35 dBm on channel 1
capture_path.usable_management_capture: hostapd -dd log plus the independent macOS scan; the same-phy monitor did not see the AP's own frames

service_checks.dnsmasq: syntax OK; with 192.168.77.1/24 on the AP interface, DHCP port 67 and DNS port 53 were bound; stopped cleanly
service_checks.radvd: syntax OK; with IPv6 forwarding enabled and 2001:db8:77::1/64 on the AP interface, it started and stopped cleanly
service_checks.openssl: s_server on 127.0.0.1:8443 started and stopped cleanly
service_checks.scapy: 2.8.0 imported and listed the AP interface
service_checks.tcpdump: captured 3 packets on the VM's eth0 as a capture sanity check

commands.command: orbctl usb attach 01130000 -m ldn; sudo modprobe -r rtw88_8822bu after a USB -110 error; orbctl usb detach/attach
commands.result: The adapter re-enumerated as <interface> (2357:0138, rtw88_8822bu, firmware 30.20.0). The first attach produced register-write -110 errors and no interface; detach/attach plus a module reload restored it.

commands.command: sudo ip link set <interface> down; sudo iw dev <interface> set type __ap; sudo ip link set <interface> up
commands.result: The adapter switched from managed to AP mode; iw reported type AP and the supported-mode list included AP and monitor.
hostapd reached AP-ENABLED on channel 1 with SSID TX10LED-NET. The macOS scan saw the SSID at -34 dBm on channel 1.
hostapd reached AP-ENABLED on channel 1 with SSID TX10LED-WPA2, derived the WPA2 PSK, and installed the group key. The macOS scan saw the SSID at -34 dBm and later -35 dBm on channel 1.

commands.command: sudo iw dev <interface> interface add <monitor> type monitor; sudo tcpdump -i <monitor> -c 80 -e -w <local.pcap>
commands.result: The monitor interface was created while the AP ran and captured 80 ambient channel-1 frames, but zero frames from the AP's BSSID and zero TX10LED frames. hostapd's debug log recorded the AP's probe RX/TX instead.

commands.command: dnsmasq --test; dnsmasq --no-daemon; radvd --configtest; radvd -n; openssl s_server; scapy get_if_list
commands.result: All host services started and stopped cleanly; the temporary IPv4/IPv6 addresses and IPv6 forwarding setting were removed/restored.

commands.command: sudo kill <hostapd>; sudo iw dev <monitor> del; sudo iw dev <interface> set type managed
commands.result: hostapd, dnsmasq, radvd, and tcpdump were stopped; the monitor interface was removed; the adapter was restored to managed mode with no test addresses.

interpretation: Phase 0 met its exit criteria without touching the console. Both the open and WPA2 APs reached AP-ENABLED on channel 1, and the independent macOS scan saw both SSIDs at -34 dBm. dnsmasq, radvd, OpenSSL, Scapy, and tcpdump all passed start/stop checks. The same-phy monitor interface can be created while the AP runs, but it does not capture the AP's own frames; management-frame attribution must therefore use hostapd's debug log and the independent scan. No malformed frame, DHCP/DNS/IPv6/TLS response, or console interaction occurred. This is feasibility evidence for D10, not a vulnerability result.
authorization: The owner approved the host-only Phase 0 setup. The test used ordinary AP beacons and probe responses, did not involve the console, and did not send malformed frames.
limitations: One adapter, one driver, one kernel, and one channel (channel 1).
The macOS scan returned nil BSSIDs for every network, so only SSID, RSSI, and channel were usable.
The same-phy monitor interface did not capture the AP's own frames; it is not a valid attribution path for injected frames on this driver.
Phase 0 did not test client association, DHCP, DNS, IPv6, or TLS with a console.
The adapter needed a USB detach/attach and module reload after an initial -110 register-write failure.
The test SSIDs and the local WPA2 passphrase are test artifacts; the passphrase is not recorded.
redactions: Interface and monitor names redacted because they are derived from the adapter MAC.
